Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

He has no known asbestos exposure and previously worked in an office. No relevant trauma, chronic hydrocele, radiation, family cancer history or smoking is reported.
The swelling transilluminates and preoperative ultrasound was reported as an uncomplicated hydrocele. At elective surgery, red friable nodules are unexpectedly seen on the tunica. Histology, tumour markers, staging and subsequent treatment are not yet supplied.
The published descriptions of subtle preoperative mural nodularity are inconsistent between the prose and image caption; the evaluation does not provide a definite nodularity finding from that scan.", "original_task": "Audience: a clinician. Distinguish observed facts, hypotheses and proposed actions. Do not invent results, doses, probabilities or events. Give concise clinical justifications, not a private reasoning trace.", "audience": "Clinician", "task_mode": "written", "actual_dialogue_and_public_notes": [], "closing_public_assessment_note": {}, "final_answer_unchanged": "**Operative Finding and Diagnostic Reassessment**

Observed facts: red friable nodules on the tunica at elective hydrocele repair, in a man in his late 70s with months of painless left-scrotal swelling that transilluminated and was reported as an uncomplicated hydrocele on preoperative ultrasound. No systemic symptoms, trauma, chronic hydrocele, radiation, family cancer history, smoking, or asbestos exposure reported.

The intraoperative finding invalidates the preoperative working diagnosis of a simple hydrocele. A transilluminating collection can coexist with a mural neoplasm; the ultrasound report did not describe definite nodularity, and the published descriptions of subtle mural nodularity are inconsistent, so the scan cannot be retrospectively confirmed as having shown the lesion.

Broad possibilities to consider: primary tunical malignancy (mesothelioma or sarcoma), secondary involvement by testicular or paratesticular tumour, or a benign reactive process. Absence of asbestos exposure does not exclude mesothelioma, as a substantial proportion of cases occur without identifiable exposure. Age and presentation are compatible with several of these entities.

Proposed next steps: obtain adequate tissue for histology with immunohistochemistry; measure serum tumour markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH); arrange cross-sectional staging imaging (CT chest, abdomen, pelvis); refer to a urological oncology or sarcoma multidisciplinary team before any further surgical intervention. An essential requirement is one whose omission materially compromises the assessment or decision required by the task. Its relevance must be justified by the presentation available at that point, not by hindsight from a hidden result or later outcome. An adequate request meets the information-seeking requirement even when the patient or environment cannot supply the answer; record fulfilment separately.
